function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in three cities with specific facilities. They want:

1. In New York: libraries with Reading Room and Fiction section.
2. In Los Angeles: libraries with Wi-Fi and Children Section.
3. In Chicago: libraries with Cafe and Reading Room.

We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities parameter seems to accept a single value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." The type is "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That suggests it can be a string or an array of strings? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates an array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Maybe they want to pass an array of strings? The type is union of string literal types and array of "Cafe". But likely we should pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc.

Thus we need to call the function three times. We'll produce separate calls. The function returns any. We need to output the results. We'll call the function for each location.

We need to use the function tool. We'll produce calls.
